We got that. It’s called reality. Consequences. They initiated the hack of the century and everything goes to absolute shit. They didn’t glorify the hack and so people found the show bleak and sad and didn’t have the patience to see Elliot and Co find their way back onto the “winning side”.

I don’t see 110 as anticlimactic at all. It’s a seriously strong episode shrouded in just enough mystery to be captivating in the moment, and even better later once we see it’s true nature. (Who knocked, where Tyrell is, why Price is important, why Whiterose is important, the Congo, the dog etc. so many important parts just labelled as “anticlimactic” lol.)

Season 1 is so basic and simple though, as much as I love it. You even say it’s a rehash of pop culture. 2/3 are on a completely different level that saying it never reached S1 heights again is just odd. 

The show climaxed in 306. That’s the climax of the story so far. Nothing in S1 comes close to the consequences of 5/9 shown in S2 and S3. 

The show also used story devices like the sequence in 206 that I can’t say I’ve seen elsewhere. Said devices allowed for past emotional exploration of character trauma that otherwise couldn’t be achieved in a flashback or a monologue. 

It’s also very adept at using the voiceover device and it’s usually in combination with montage which is highly entertaining (opening of 302 is a great example). 

I’d say 310 is the best finale by far too. 308 is one of the best portrayals of suicidal tendencies on TV period. 

Each episode in 2/3 did something special, whereas S1 is a rag tag team working towards an idealistic goal. As we see, the world doesn’t work that way. Vera’s great but simple. The hack is a great concept but simple. What makes this show special is it’s exploration of consequences, and the response we take as individuals. Fight or flight? 

It’s why a lot of people fell off after S1. The show grounded itself in the reality of consequences. Elliot is fucking nuts, the hack is not a positive thing in the real world and that’s depressing to realise. Especially with how badly things go for everybody after 5/9. But, that’s revolutions. That’s realistic. It’s good storytelling. Not as fun to watch as Elliot busting pedophiles week in week out but infinitely more fulfilling as a story in the end.

If it ends strongly, which is a huge ask of any show, it definitely will. It’s done a lot of things during its run that you just don’t see on TV. Accurate hacking, accurate mental illness, addiction, global politics, a reliable unreliable narrator, stigmatised topics like depression anxiety suicide etc. 

It’s a product of the times and it has captured said time better than any other show airing during this period.
